record.category: contributed storage - hosted indexer over third-party hosts

free_tier.stated: Free plan 50 GB, 3 apps, 500 Mbps. Plus USD 7.99/mo: 500 GB, 10 apps, 500 Mbps. Pro USD 14.99/mo: 5 TB, 25 apps, 1 Gbps. Unlimited USD 19.99/mo: 10 TB, 100 apps, 5 Gbps, plus USD 4.99/TB-month for each TB stored above 10 TB. Plan volumes are decimal GB and TB as the plan table states them, not binary.
free_tier.notes: the plan table read on 2026-11-01; the included volumes are decimal GB and TB, and the tier above 10 TB bills USD 4.99/TB-month

per_object_cap.stated: Through s3d the largest single object is built from multipart uploads of parts of up to 5 GiB and up to 10,000 parts per upload; the resulting ceiling is far above every plan volume the offer sells. No page states a cap for the SDK upload path.
per_object_cap.notes: the multipart ceiling belongs to the s3d S3 route; the SDK and app routes state no per-object cap, and every plan volume is reached first

retention.stated: Trashed files are deleted permanently 30 days after they are trashed, and the storage they used is freed the next time the app runs and syncs. No page states a deletion clock for live objects: they are stored until trashed, until the account is deleted, or until the account is signed out with local data cleared, which keeps the account and the uploaded files.
retention.notes: the 30-day clock applies to objects that are trashed; deleting an account, from the app menu, permanently deletes the account and everything stored with it

egress.terms: Each plan states a transfer speed cap (500 Mbps on Free and Plus, 1 Gbps on Pro, 5 Gbps on Unlimited) and the pricing page lists no per-GB egress price and no egress allowance.

record.interface_detail: The S3 route is s3d, a gateway the user installs and runs on their own machine (macOS, Linux, Windows or Docker) and points at a Sia Storage account; the s3d page calls it 's3d is a self-hosted gateway that speaks the S3 API'. The Sia Storage app for iOS and Android is the other client, and SDKs exist for Rust, Go, Python and JavaScript.
record.tooling: rclone, Cyberduck, Nextcloud, Synology Hyper Backup, Arq, AWS CLI - all named on the s3d page
record.chaining: s3d on a $3 VPS + rclone = an S3 endpoint whose bytes live on 530 independent hosts; put Cloudflare in front and egress becomes CF's problem
record.limits_note: The plan table is the price: USD 19.99/mo for 10 TB, then USD 4.99 per TB-month for each TB above it, billed in decimal TB, so 20 TiB (21.99 TB) costs USD 79.82/mo. The free plan is 50 GB. Speed is a per-plan cap: 500 Mbps on Free and Plus, 1 Gbps on Pro, 5 Gbps on Unlimited.

identity_cost.detail: email: the Sia Storage Company login page asks for an Email address and links a Sign up page, and the free plan is documented as needing no Siacoin to buy and no server to run; what the signup form asks beyond the email is unverified

record.reliability_note: Data is erasure-coded across many independent storage providers and repaired when redundancy drops, so the offer depends on those providers staying online. Siascan reported 2.26 PB of storage utilisation against 7.51 PB of provider capacity across 522 active hosts.
record.confidence_note: the plan table and its speed caps, the S3 route through s3d and siascan's network figures are quoted from captured pages read on 2026-11-01, each page carrying its own evidence row

card.summary: 50 GB free. 'The free plan includes 50 GB of storage, up to 3 connected apps, and transfer speeds up to 524 Mbps — with no Siacoin to buy and no server to ru...

free_tier.stated: 50 GB free. 'The free plan includes 50 GB of storage, up to 3 connected apps, and transfer speeds up to 524 Mbps — with no Siacoin to buy and no server to run.'.

egress.terms: unmetered but rate-shaped by plan: 'transfer speeds up to 524 Mbps' on Free. No per-GB egress line item exists in Sia's model.

record.tooling: s3d gateway (github.com/SiaFoundation/s3d) exposes an S3-compatible API; docs name Rclone and Cyberduck explicitly. Python/Go/Rust/JS SDKs also exist. rclone has a native 'sia' backend (rclone.org/sia/).
record.chaining: 50 GB x unlimited accounts (signup is free, no Siacoin required). The plan gate is '3 connected apps' per account, and an app is a token. The same wrapper pattern as Google service accounts. 400 accounts = 20 TB, but each is a separate signup.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: not stated on the pages read. request-rate / per-ip-shaping: 'transfer speeds up to 524 Mbps' is the explicit Free-plan throttle. retention: not stated; storage is contract-based, so retention is paid-for duration, not decaying.
record.reliability_note: New hosted product (app launched 2026); only paths offered on the free page are the iOS/Android app and the s3d gateway, so scripting depends entirely on s3d working.
